editorial_thesis: Boundaries became checkable today: machine-gated math releases, side channels inside shared inference servers, a live supply-chain incident on the agent store shelf, and consent engineered into consumer agent UX.

topic_groups.title: Formal Math Goes Mainstream
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Nov 23 covered the GRH verification story; today the release pattern went multi-lab (two OpenAI preprints with Lean proofs, a 154x compact rewrite with independent MIT verification), and an independent developer ported the method to ordinary software (17 unreported Clojure bugs). Material update, not a repeat.

sources.title: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths (OpenAI preprint + Lean)
sources.why_selected: Serious omega bound published as paper + Lean formalization in one commit; the checker-gated release pattern now spans two labs.
sources.usefulness: Template for verification-first artifact delivery in Buildn/client work.

sources.title: Superpolynomial graph diameter of simple polytopes (Hirsch conjecture false)
sources.why_selected: Second same-day OpenAI preprint confirming the release pattern is deliberate, not a one-off.
sources.usefulness: Signals the norm; watch who formalizes next.

sources.title: grh-lean: much shorter GRH proof from Anthropic (lsernau)
sources.why_selected: 17M-line GRH proof rewritten to ~76k compact lines, same five theorems, independently verified at MIT on two machines.
sources.usefulness: Best current case study of AI-assisted compression with a checker still green; legacy-refactor pitch material.

sources.title: MIT verification files for the shorter GRH Lean proof
sources.why_selected: Independent verification record incl. paranoid comparator runs; the accountability layer of the story.
sources.usefulness: Proof-of-verification pattern for client deliverables.

sources.title: 17 unreported bugs in Clojure core found via Lean + differential testing
sources.why_selected: Proves the formal-methods loop works on ordinary application code (vector-of infinite loop present since 2010, found by bv_decide).
sources.usefulness: Direct service offer: model arithmetic-dense client modules in Lean, ship counterexamples.

sources.title: ProofAtlas: top 500 open math problems by LLM-assessed importance
sources.why_selected: Complements a week of big proof news with a navigation/selection tool; its useful-failures ledger is a stealable pattern.
sources.usefulness: Research scoping; ledger design for Buildn OS agent workflows.

topic_groups.title: Agent Compartment Breach
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Yesterday's platform-trust lane was external; today's signal is internal — side channels inside shared inference servers hit the HN front page (#4, 458 pts) the same day a 12-year-old pre-auth kernel root and a live cloud-takeover study surfaced. Fresh lane name, no overlap with Nov 14 security-monitoring coverage.

sources.title: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
sources.why_selected: Demonstrates covert channels (kernel choice, shared KV cache) between sandboxed agents plus a colluding-monitor result (354/354 attacks passed); serving layer is now an agent-security surface.
sources.usefulness: Drives cache-separation and compartment design in any multi-tenant agent serving plan.

sources.title: side-channel-communication code
sources.why_selected: Reproducible code behind the LessWrong write-up.
sources.usefulness: Hands-on study of serving-layer leakage.

sources.title: NFS2ROOT: CVE-2026-99362 pre-auth remote root in Linux nfsd
sources.why_selected: CVSS 9.8, 12 years old, and the exploit chain was completed end-to-end by an AI harness (Antara); patch latency is the whole defense.
sources.usefulness: Immediate nfsd/2049 exposure audit on all managed Linux hosts.

sources.title: Slow Ubuntu security response times (oss-security)
sources.why_selected: Documents multi-day/week gaps for remote kernel corruptions on Ubuntu LTS; distro choice becomes a patch-latency decision.
sources.usefulness: Informs base-image kernel strategy for Buildn infra.

sources.title: Taking over US Treasury subdomains for $3 each
sources.why_selected: 28 live EIP takeovers from 450k IP allocations in 48h; AWS ban trivially bypassed via account transfer; dangling DNS is now an automated exploit.
sources.usefulness: One-hour dangling-record sweep deliverable for client AWS zones.

sources.title: 1Password Nov 2026 security incident update
sources.why_selected: Zero-knowledge design held; entry vector was an employee GitHub account pushing code to backend services — same family as the Nx credential-stealer wave.
sources.usefulness: Push-rights and CI/CD secret policy updates for Buildn and clients.

topic_groups.title: Voice Agents Get a Cheap Brain
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Voice/edge last ran Nov 11 (self-hosted local voice); today brings the hosted middle ground with open weights inside the telephony network, plus a regulatory deadline (FCC vote Dec 17). New production-economics datapoint, not a repeat of the local-stack angle.

sources.title: Gemma 4 31B now available for Telnyx Voice AI assistants
sources.why_selected: Open-weight Google model as a selectable LLM slot next to telephony: $0.32/$1.20 per 1M tokens, 12 languages, US+UAE hosting, Apache 2.0.
sources.usefulness: Multilingual voice agent (Arabic+English) is now a config, not a project; direct fit for lead-gen work.

sources.title: Gemma 4 on Telnyx: what the release means for voice buyers
sources.why_selected: Independent buyer-side read: token prices are not call prices; six questions to ask any voice vendor.
sources.usefulness: Vendor-evaluation checklist for client voice rollouts.

sources.title: FCC robocall-blocking proposal: December 17 vote
sources.why_selected: Regulation is moving at capability pace; likelihood-of-illegality blocking shifts burden to deployers.
sources.usefulness: Compliance-by-design requirement for any outbound voice agent.

sources.title: PenGPT: a generative transformer for handwriting and sketches
sources.why_selected: HN #9 with 399 pts; 80%-data/15%-speed/5%-architecture lesson in a runnable browser demo.
sources.usefulness: Small-model demo for client sessions; signature/sketch personalization option.

sources.title: Serving Qwen via 5,600 Lambdas for fun and 80x negative profit
sources.why_selected: Clean negative result ($8.40 vs $0.10 per 1M tokens) that proves why serving infrastructure exists; shows open models are approachable as ordinary software.
sources.usefulness: Cost sanity-check teaching material; supports boundary-layer-first design in Env Vault.

topic_groups.title: Agents on the Store Shelf
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Yesterday's whose-agent-is-it lane was about policy ownership; today the store shelf itself made news: a live malicious-package incident in an agent framework, consumer agent checkout at Walmart for Black Friday, and Cloudflare's agent discoverability endpoint. Agentic commerce last covered Nov 16 — material updates only.

sources.title: Microsoft Agent Framework: malicious PyPI uploads of 1.26.1/1.26.2
sources.why_selected: First incident where an agent-framework package was the credential-stealing vehicle, executing at interpreter startup in agent sandboxes and CI.
sources.usefulness: Immediate lockfile/CI audit; standing provenance + SBOM gates for anything agents install.

sources.title: Walmart opens its Agent Gateway to Meta's Muse for Black Friday
sources.why_selected: First consumer-scale third-party agent checkout flow at peak retail; UK Muse rollout same week with Stripe-built Link wallet and required purchase approval.
sources.usefulness: Retail clients need an agent-profile spec (scoped payment, audit, no PII resale) now.

sources.title: Cloudflare Search for Agents (/.well-known/search)
sources.why_selected: One-click agent discoverability with a Markdown contract replaces brittle scraping; owner controls exposure.
sources.usefulness: Enable on a staging domain and point a coding agent at docs this week.

topic_groups.title: Craft, Care, and the Web
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Fills two coverage gaps in one lane: platform/engineering culture (untouched since Nov 20) and front-end craft (untouched since early Nov). Three HN front-page items with direct, practical takeaways.

sources.title: Smart People Who Give a Shit Use Tools (Ian Duncan)
sources.why_selected: Best-articulated rebuttal to the 'AI robs engineers of care' argument: caring was rationed by typing speed, and the tool makes rigorous verification cheap for those who already care.
sources.usefulness: Pitch language and review-gate rationale for Buildn OS.

sources.title: Bypassing iOS Safari's 60 FPS limit to feel native
sources.why_selected: 118 FPS via compositor-side scroll reads without dev flags; first broadly applicable PWA escape on iOS.
sources.usefulness: Targeted fix for the worst-feeling mobile interaction in client products.

sources.title: Button Sounds (Josh W. Comeau)
sources.why_selected: HN #3, 864 pts; 50+ multi-sampled UI sounds, free, npm, self-hostable, agent-friendly docs.
sources.usefulness: Half-hour sound-feedback upgrade for dashboards; docs pattern for AI-policy-aware sites.

sources.title: pw-loudness-eq: Windows loudness DSP ported to PipeWire
sources.why_selected: Faithful reverse-engineering of a Windows-only audio feature, per-app loudness on Linux, clean module split.
sources.usefulness: Install on the Linux workstation; case-study pattern for behavior-porting work.

topic_groups.title: Everyday Agents, Everyday Consent
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Rotates away from yesterday's infrastructure emphasis into product/protocol surface: MCP gained the exact primitives Buildn OS encodes (tasks, gates, skills), consumer agents started calling businesses with engineered disclosure, and enterprise platforms shipped first-class agent identity. Consent-at-the-boundary is the unifying frame.

sources.title: Anthropic MCP update: server Skills, long-running Tasks, Elicitation, File Uploads
sources.why_selected: MCP now carries procedure, resumable async work, approval pauses, and context-bypassing file transfer — direct protocol alignment with Buildn OS task/workflow design.
sources.usefulness: Prototype one MCP-backed skill for a repeatable client procedure.

sources.title: Gemini Duplex returns: Gemini calls businesses for you
sources.why_selected: Consumer-scale agent calling with built-in AI disclosure and business opt-out; consent engineered into the call.
sources.usefulness: Disclosure-and-exit pattern for any agent acting toward third parties.

sources.title: Enterprise agent identity: agents as first-class org members
sources.why_selected: Agents get their own manager, narrow scope, and full audit trail; capability separates from access — the structural answer to yesterday's ownership question.
sources.usefulness: Scoped agent access model for Buildn OS and Env Vault.
